text:
On 1 May 2026 the remember-what-survived pattern was posted as a live Python critical-path optimizer. Not a static Gantt chart. A plan already in motion, with real commitments locked in. When reality changes, most systems either throw the whole plan away or bolt a patch onto too much of the old one. Both fail.

Preserve what remains coherent. Deform what is stressed. Reset only what became stale. Same three moves as the protein and TSP labs.

The 1 May live critical-path post is an applied transfer of the remember-what-survived operator into a plan already in motion. It is not a unification proof and not a product claim.

A plan already in motion

The post lists quantum, fractal growth, Villin HP35, and Great Grok Challenge holdouts as rhyming domains and says it is not a proof. The live lab on this atlas is a teaching DAG: inject a shock (design slip, blocked core, integrate rewrite) and compare restart-from-zero, patch-everything, and recover.

The best next plan is not always the shortest new plan. It is the one that improves the future without destroying the valid past.

I’m not saying this proves anything but I am saying the recurrence is getting impossible to ignore. Survival doesn’t always restart from zero. It often optimizes by remembering what endured — and pruning the rest.

Python

def recover(G, R, shock, tau_lo=0.25, tau_hi=0.72):
    stress = strain(G, R, shock)          # visible gap × forgotten history
    keep   = G[stress < tau_lo]           # preserve coherent commitments
    warp   = deform(G[(stress >= tau_lo) & (stress < tau_hi)], R)
    reseed = reset(G[stress >= tau_hi])   # only the stale
    return splice(keep, warp, reseed)

The critical-path video lives on X. There is no required Tmp/TOE folder. The browser lab is a reconstruction of the posted three-way split, not a product optimizer and not a schedule solver championship.

What this does not show

Not a Gantt replacement product and not a claim that recover beats PERT/CPM on industry suites.
Not a unification theorem with protein folding or fractal TSP — recurrence is the open question.
Not gravity. χ ≈ 0.2667 is not a universal applied-lab constant on this atlas.

Whether protein, TSP, critical path, and C3++ share one operator — and whether that operator is the quadratic-RG χ — remains an open question. Recurrence across posted Python labs is not a closed unification law.
